newsitem.title: USA: Argentina industry seen strong, job growth slow.
newsitem.headline: Argentina industry seen strong, job growth slow.

text.p: Argentine Industry Secretary Alieto Guadagni said Thursday the country's industrial recovery was firmly based, but its high unemployment rate would not drop significantly until the final quarter of 1997.
Guadagni told Reuters Financial Television the official figure for last month's industrial production would show a rise of more than 11 percent compared with October 1995.
"The official figure for October will be something greater than 11 percent," Guadagni said. "The recession is behind us. From this point we hope to reduce the level of unemployment."
On Wednesday, independent Argentine consultancy FIEL reported an 11.7 percent rise in October industrial output.
Industrial output should increase next year and account for a larger share of exports than the current level of 60 percent, he said.
"The automobile industry will increase its output next year along with agro-business and petrochemcials," he said. "We are having a full recovery in housing construction."

The minister said higher industrial production and an accelerated recovery would help lower the unemployment rate, which stood at 17.1 percent in May, but that major reform of labor legislation was needed to boost job creation.
"We have unemployment that was due to structural adjustment of our economy," he said. "We have to wait for some time before we reduce the level of unemployment."
Argentina should see economic growth soak up joblessness by the fourth quarter of 1997, Guadagni said.
"I am confident that by next year by now (Q4), we will have the full benefits of economic expansion," he said.
He called for greater labor flexibility, a new legal framework to promote job creation, as well as lower taxes to spark demand for new workers.
He did give any figures to what level unemployment would drop.
Guadagni pointed to recovery in demand for durable consumer goods across industrial sectors.
"There are certain industries associated with capital goods that have a very high level of activity such as the steel and the automobile industries," Guadagni said.
"We are going to have record output of oil and gas, and we are going to have a record crop," he added.
The minister said the main factors driving economic growth, which rose 6.6 percent in the third quarter year-over-year, were exports and foreign investment.

Guadagni, who arrived in New York after traveling to Europe and Japan, said the Frankfurt and Paris airport authorities will take part in open bidding for Argentina's airport operations, due to be privatized next year.
